.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
No changes to the forecast.

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Above normal temperatures and dry conditions through
  Wednesday with increasing rain chances Thursday into early

- 2) Rain chances continue into early next week with cooling

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Above normal temperatures and dry conditions
through Wednesday with increasing rain chances Thursday into 
early next week.

High pressure will keep the region dry late this afternoon,
through tonight and most of the day Wednesday. A light southeast
to southerly flow will bring in additional moisture and some
warmth throughout this prolonged period. As a matter of fact,
the increasing moisture and falling temperatures at night could
result in some patchy fog in interior mountain valleys and along
and east of the Blue Ridge Mountains. Otherwise, mostly sunny
skies expected through midday Wednesday, before some increasing
clouds in the afternoon. Lows tonight will fall back into the 
upper 40s and low 50s with highs back in the low to mid 70s 
Wednesday. A few locations could punch into the upper 70s in the
lee of Alleghenies and south/east of Washington DC Wednesday 
afternoon given increased southerly flow. 

The high pressure ridge will break down to allow for increasing
clouds and increasing rain chances from west to east Wednesday
night. Lesser rain chances on Thursday as a trough moves by to
the north. The resultant surface front is set to cross sometime
Thursday morning into Thursday afternoon leading to scattered 
showers and a few t-storms. Rainfall amounts Thursday will range
between a tenth to a quarter of an inch with locally higher 
totals west of the Alleghenies where better forcing resides. 
Despite increased cloud cover expect highs back into the low to 
mid 70s (60s mountains) Thursday afternoon. Storm total rain 
through Friday night will generally be between a quarter to a 
half an inch. 


KEY MESSAGE 2...Rain chances continue into early next week with
cooling temperatures.

Temperatures drop towards the beginning of the weekend as Thursday's 
cold front passes offshore, with afternoon highs back in the 60s on 
Saturday. Skies could temporarily clear Saturday afternoon into 
Sunday as the earlier upper-level trough continues east. Meanwhile, 
a second trough moving southeast from the Canadian Rockies will move 
in closely behind, with a stemming cold front moving through 
beginning late Sunday into Monday. This second upper level low could 
bring additional rain showers to the region, although total QPF 
estimates continue to be uncertain. Thunderstorm potential should be 
lower with this second wave, and any rainfall will continue to be 
beneficial after 2+ weeks in a dry spell. 

Temperatures continue to cool towards more seasonable November 
normals, with highs in the low-60s over the metros and low-50s in 
the mountains by Monday. Overnight lows could return to the mid-to-
low 30s in some areas early next week as these cold fronts move 
through. Zonal flow overhead returns by midweek next week. 

&&

.AVIATION /19Z TUESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
VFR conditions and light south/southeasterly winds at less than
15 kts will continue through Wednesday as high pressure 
meanders over the western Atlantic. Some patchy fog could occur
again along and east of I-95 tonight/Wednesday morning given 
the uptick in moisture advection. This will lead to brief 
reductions in cigs/vsbys during the 9-13z/4-8am time window. 
VFR conditions continue into Thursday although brief sub-VFR 
reductions are possible at times with showers and even a few 
thunderstorms Thursday morning into Thursday afternoon. South to
southwesterly winds continue at less than 15 kts. 

Temporary restrictions could linger throughout the day Friday 
as continued rain showers track through the Mid-Atlantic. 
Conditions should improve throughout the day Saturday, with 
winds flowing northwesterly in the wake of the front. VFR 
conditions for most of the weekend, with additional rain showers
possible beginning late Sunday into Monday as a second cold 
front pushes through. 

&&

.MARINE...
No marine hazards are expected through Wednesday morning. Winds will 
remain light out of the south and southeast through Wednesday as 
high pressure pushes offshore. By Wednesday evening into Thursday 
morning, expect the potential for southerly channeling due to the 
high offshore and incumbent trough from the northern Ohio River 
Valley. Confidence in this occurring is low with a focus over the 
middle and open waters. 

Winds shift northwesterly on Saturday in the wake of a cold 
front, potentially crossing SCA thresholds by the afternoon. Winds 
temporarily diminish on Sunday evening before increasing to 20 
knot gusts ahead of a second cold front on Monday.
